scenario_name: Pilot-scale spray drying of neutralized protein concentrate
key_process_conditions: T_in=160 C; T_out target=75 C; two-fluid nozzle; feed=10 mL/min equivalent scale-normalized
quality_model: thermal Arrhenius + interface exposure + surface enrichment
energy_model: air heating + blower + atomizer + product collection losses
validation_targets: Plant-protein infeed 10-25%; inlet 130-195 C; outlet 60-97 C; pilot yield 60-80%
recommended_use: Primary economical drying scenario for scale-up and TEA
assumption_statement: Grass-protein transport, denaturation, sorption and cyclone parameters are bounded assumptions.
warnings: Do not use inlet temperature alone as protein temperature; integrate droplet temperature history.

scenario_name: Low-temperature spray drying for functionality retention
key_process_conditions: T_in=130 C; T_out=60-70 C; higher feed rate; high air flow
quality_model: reduced thermal damage with increased moisture/stickiness risk
validation_targets: Low outlet temperature and acceptable moisture; product solubility retained
recommended_use: Sensitivity alternative when functionality is prioritized
assumption_statement: Tradeoff between reduced thermal damage and reduced drying/collection efficiency is assumed.
warnings: May increase wall sticking, residual moisture and storage instability.

scenario_name: Conservative freeze drying of protein concentrate
key_process_conditions: cooling 0.5 K/min to -45 C; primary shelf -30 C; chamber 0.093 mbar; secondary 20 C for 4 h
quality_model: two-state freezing stability + interface denaturation + over-drying penalty
validation_targets: Product temperature below collapse minus 3 K; residual moisture not driven far below activity-safe range
recommended_use: High-quality reference scenario and laboratory-product route
assumption_statement: Collapse temperature, cake resistance and grass-protein stability constants are assumptions until measured.
warnings: Pharmaceutical-protein parameters are used as generic priors, not direct grass-protein constants.

key_process_conditions: slow cooling 0.1-0.3 K/min; high nucleation temperature; optional annealing
energy_model: freeze-dryer energy model with longer freezing but faster primary drying
validation_targets: Larger ice crystals, lower interface area and lower cake resistance
recommended_use: Sensitivity case for proteins stable in bulk but sensitive to interfaces
assumption_statement: Protein-stability class is unknown and treated as scenario selection.
warnings: Slow cooling is not universally optimal.

key_process_conditions: fast cooling 0.8-1.0 K/min; minimize time in low-viscosity cold region
validation_targets: Short freezing duration and acceptable native-protein retention
recommended_use: Opposite sensitivity case required by freezing-stability paper
assumption_statement: Used because grass-protein bulk cold stability is not known.
warnings: Fast cooling increases ice-water interface area and may harm surface-sensitive proteins.
